questions.question: What is the primary focus of kinematics?
options: Describing the current state of a system
Calculating the forces acting on a body
Analyzing the rotation of rigid bodies
questions.answer: Describing the current state of a system
questions.explanation: Kinematics is defined as the complete description of the present state of a system, focusing on what it is doing rather than why.
questions.flashcard_back: A complete description of a system's current state of motion.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Kinematics describes the 'what' of motion, such as position and speed, without addressing the 'why'.

questions.question: A mathematical point particle has no spatial extent.
questions.explanation: The lecturer defines a mathematical point as an entity that has no size or spatial extent.
questions.flashcard_front: Does a mathematical point particle have spatial extent?
questions.flashcard_back: No, it has no size or spatial extent.
questions.flashcard_explanation: It is an idealized point used to simplify mechanics by ignoring rotation and internal structure.

questions.question: What is the simplest way to visualize one-dimensional motion?
questions.answer: A bead with a wire going through it that can only slide back and forth.
questions.explanation: The lecturer uses the analogy of a bead on a wire to illustrate motion constrained to a single dimension.
questions.flashcard_back: A bead sliding back and forth on a wire.
questions.flashcard_explanation: This analogy represents the simplest possible constraint for motion along a single line.

questions.question: How does dynamics differ from kinematics?
questions.answer: Dynamics explains the reasons behind motion (the 'why'), whereas kinematics only describes the current state of motion.
questions.explanation: Kinematics describes the present state, while dynamics explains the forces that cause changes to that state.
questions.flashcard_front: What is the difference between kinematics and dynamics?
questions.flashcard_back: Kinematics describes motion; dynamics explains why motion changes.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Kinematics is descriptive (the 'what'), while dynamics is explanatory (the 'why').
